([[Huntington Beach, California]]) | college = [[UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball|UC Irvine]] (2013–2016) | draft_year = 2016 | career_start = 2018 | career_end = 2020 | career_position = [[Center (basketball)|Center]] | career_number = | years1 = 2018 | team1 = [[Fuerza Regia de Monterrey]] | years2 = 2019–2020 | team2 = [[Correcaminos UAT Victoria]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[Big West Conference|Big West]] (2016) * 2× Big West Defensive Player of the Year (2014, 2016) * First-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2013) }} '''Mamadou N'Diaye''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|m|ɑː|m|ə|d|uː|_|ˈ|ɛ|n|dʒ|aɪ}} {{respell|MAH|mə|doo|_|EN|jy}}; born 14 September 1993) is a Senegalese former professional [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for [[UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball|UC Irvine]], where he was the tallest basketball player at the [[Division I (NCAA)|NCAA Division I]] level, standing at {{height|ft=7|in=6}}.{{cite magazine|last1=Machir|first1=Troy|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson posterizes the tallest player in the nation|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2014-11-19/rondae-hollis-jefferson-dunk-video-mamadou-ndiaye|magazine=Sporting News|access-date=22 November 2014|date=19 November 2014|archive-date=22 November 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141122175640/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2014-11-19/rondae-hollis-jefferson-dunk-video-mamadou-ndiaye|url-status=live}}{{cite news|last1=Eisenberg|first1=Jeff|title=Rondae Hollis-Jefferson dunks on college hoops' tallest player|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaab-the-dagger/rondae-hollis-jefferson-dunks-on-college-basketball-s-tallest-player-171549960.html|work=Yahoo Sports|access-date=22 November 2014|date=20 November 2014|archive-date=2 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141202053926/http://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaab-the-dagger/rondae-hollis-jefferson-dunks-on-college-basketball-s-tallest-player-171549960.html|url-status=live}} N'Diaye, a [[center (basketball)|center]], was named [[Big West Conference]] Defensive Player of the Year after the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]] and earned all-conference honorable mention accolades as well. He was considered a talented [[block (basketball)|shot-blocker]].{{cite web|title=Men's Basketball: UCI's Ndiaye coming back|url=http://www.dailypilot.com/sports/tn-dpt-sp-0415-mamadou-ndiaye-staying-20150414,0,5604990.story|website=[[Daily Pilot]]|date=15 April 2015|access-date=28 April 2015|archive-date=8 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908090852/http://www.dailypilot.com/sports/tn-dpt-sp-0415-mamadou-ndiaye-staying-20150414,0,5604990.story|url-status=live}} N'Diaye played professionally for [[Fuerza Regia de Monterrey]] and [[Correcaminos UAT Victoria]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]] (LNBP). He is also one of the [[List of tallest people|tallest living humans]]. == Early life == N'Diaye was born in [[Dakar]], [[Senegal]]. He had an older brother.{{cite web|title=Mamadou Ndiaye Bio|url=http://www.ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/bios/ndiaye_mamadou_vy9a|website=UCIrvineSports.com|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=6 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006213324/http://www.ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/bios/ndiaye_mamadou_vy9a|url-status=live}} He grew up playing soccer and did not seriously begin playing basketball at a young age. In 2010, Amadou Koundoul, who was the assistant coach for the [[UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball]] team at the time, saw N'Diaye participate in a [[pick-up game]] in a gymnasium at Dakar. He asked him to travel to the [[United States]], and N'Diaye accepted the offer.{{cite web|last1=Kaufman|first1=Joey|title=The Burden of 7-6|url=http://www.sportsonearth.com/article/67717370/uc-irvine-7-foot-6-center-mamadou-ndiaye-discusses-challenges|publisher=SportsOnEarth|access-date=22 November 2014|date=13 February 2014|archive-date=15 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150915152218/http://www.sportsonearth.com/article/67717370/uc-irvine-7-foot-6-center-mamadou-ndiaye-discusses-challenges|url-status=dead}} He arrived in the US without knowing how to speak English. In the new country, he initially had trouble with speaking [[English language|English]] and often needed things to be translated to [[French language|French]]. After experiencing headaches upon his arrival to the U.S., N'Diaye saw a doctor and it was discovered that he was suffering from a golf ball-sized [[pituitary tumour|tumor]] in his [[pituitary gland]], which had caused gigantism and was threatening his vision. Afterwards, he recalled the moment, "For me, it wasn’t a big deal because I didn’t know what a tumor was. Once I found out, it was tough to hear I had one."{{cite web|last1=Bi|first1=Rakesh|title=Mamadou Ndiaye: Even at 7-6, Winning Isn't Always Easy|url=http://www.truschoolsports.com/2015/03/mamadou-ndiaye-even-at-7-6-winning-isnt-always-easy/|website=TruSchoolSports.com|access-date=28 April 2015|archive-date=21 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150521112757/http://www.truschoolsports.com/2015/03/mamadou-ndiaye-even-at-7-6-winning-isnt-always-easy/|url-status=live}} The condition was treated in the [[Hoag (health network)|Hoag Memorial Hospital]] following several charitable donations from around the area. A married couple who lived in [[Huntington Beach, California]], a city close to N'Diaye's future school, offered to become his guardians to ease his commute for medical treatments.{{cite news|last1=DiGiovanna|first1=Mike|title=UC Irvine center Mamadou Ndiaye creates altering reality for opponents|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-xpm-2014-jan-14-la-sp-0114-mamadou-ndiaye-irvine-20140114-21-story.html|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|date=14 January 2014|access-date=4 October 2014|archive-date=6 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006221318/http://articles.latimes.com/2014/jan/14/sports/la-sp-0114-mamadou-ndiaye-irvine-20140114-21|url-status=live}}{{cite web|last1=Johnson|first1=Bailey|title=Mamadou Ndiaye, 7-foot-5 high school basketball player|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/news/mamadou-ndiaye-7-foot-5-high-school-basketball-player/|publisher=CBS News|date=9 February 2012|access-date=9 October 2014|archive-date=16 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016103851/http://www.cbsnews.com/news/mamadou-ndiaye-7-foot-5-high-school-basketball-player/|url-status=live}} == High school career == Prior to participating in sports, N'Diaye attended Stoneridge Prep in [[Simi Valley, California]], who steered him through his early years in the [[United States]]. The school had a history of producing high-caliber international basketball players, including [[Enes Kanter]] and [[Nikola Vučević]]. However, N'Diaye was not allowed to play the sport during his first year in the high school because of [[California Interscholastic Federation]] rules.{{#tag:ref|The [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) requires foreign students to sit out one year before taking part in athletics.{{cite web|last1=Ceglinsky|first1=Sean|title=Ndiaye a curious mystery in many ways|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/preps/post/_/id/14965/ndiaye-a-curious-mystery-in-many-ways|publisher=ESPN|date=2 February 2012|access-date=16 September 2014|archive-date=29 November 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129070024/http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/preps/post/_/id/14965/ndiaye-a-curious-mystery-in-many-ways|url-status=live}}|group=lower-alpha}} As a sophomore, he was officially granted the permission to transfer to another high school. {{quote box |quote="It was all I knew– California and UC Irvine. And the beach reminds me of Senegal." |source=—N'Diaye after traveling to the US{{cite web|last1=Dougherty|first1=Jesse|title=Ndiaye adapts to American game, shines as 7-foot-6 freshman at UC Irvine|url=http://www.dailyorange.com/2014/02/ndiaye-adapts-to-american-game-shines-as-7-foot-6-freshman-at-uc-irvine/|website=DailyOrange.com|date=17 February 2014|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=2 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140902191755/http://dailyorange.com/2014/02/ndiaye-adapts-to-american-game-shines-as-7-foot-6-freshman-at-uc-irvine/|url-status=live}} |width=20em |align=right}} N'Diaye attended [[Brethren Christian Junior/Senior High School|Brethren Christian School]] in Huntington Beach, California. He played under head coach Jon Bahnsen. According to Bahnsen upon arriving at the school, N'Diaye "could barely get up and down the court more than a few times" due to his poor fitness after rehabilitation. In his high school years, N'Diaye, who stood {{height|ft=7|in=5}} at the time, was considered one of the tallest to play at that level. He was also approached by the [[Guinness World Records]] to determine the authenticity of the claims.{{cite news|last1=Smith|first1=Cameron|title=7-foot-5 Senegalese teen Mamadou Ndiaye is dominating California prep hoops|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/highschool-prep-rally/7-foot-5-senegalese-teen-mamadou-ndiaye-dominating-201311480.html|work=Yahoo Sports|date=20 January 2012|access-date=9 October 2014|archive-date=17 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141017185902/http://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/highschool-prep-rally/7-foot-5-senegalese-teen-mamadou-ndiaye-dominating-201311480.html|url-status=live}} Bahnsen said, "Our school wouldn't cooperate with them, but Guinness probably wanted to see if he was the world's tallest high school basketball player."{{cite web|title=This 7ft 5in H.S. Basketball Player is Right Here in SoCal|url=http://www.lobshots.com/2012/01/27/this-7ft-5in-h-s-basketball-player-is-right-here-in-socal/|website=LobShots.com|date=27 January 2012|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=14 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141014210316/http://www.lobshots.com/2012/01/27/this-7ft-5in-h-s-basketball-player-is-right-here-in-socal/|url-status=live}} As a junior at Brethren Christian, N'Diaye finished the season averaging 24 points and 14 rebounds. [[CBS News]] wrote that he was "impossible to defend" because of his height. At the conclusion of his final, senior season with Brethren Christian, N'Diaye averaged about 27 points, 14 rebounds, and 4.5 blocks. He partook his highest-scoring game in January 2013 against [[Oxford Academy (California)|Oxford Academy]], with 45 points and 15 rebounds coming off an illness that kept him out of the initial games. After the year, N'Diaye earned All-State honors and was named CIF-5AA Player of the Year. He also earned the 2013 John R. Wooden High School Player of the Year award for CIF Division V. In the same season, N'Diaye garnered National Christian Schools Athletic Association Player of the Year and Far West Super-Region team accolades. Also, he was named Academy League Most Valuable Player. According to the [[ESPN]] Recruiting Nation, N'Diaye was the 6th most promising high school player in his state. ESPN analysts commented on N'Diaye's basketball talent by saying, "Ndiaye is a legit 7-foot-5 prospect with extraordinary length and huge hands."{{cite web|title=Mamadou Ndiaye Basketball Recruiting|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/evaluation/_/id/149059/mamadou-ndiaye|website=ESPN.com|access-date=9 October 2014|archive-date=8 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141008130102/http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/evaluation/_/id/149059/mamadou-ndiaye|url-status=live}} He officially committed to play with the [[UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball]] team, following matriculation at the [[University of California, Irvine]], on 14 November 2012. He also considered [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], and [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]]. N'Diaye said that he selected UC Irvine because he "felt very comfortable at the university and with the coaching staff."{{cite web|title=Mamadou Ndiaye, 7-5 Center, Signs with UC Irvine|url=http://ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2012-13/releases/201211154w0dbc|website=UCIrvineSports.com|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=19 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140819220844/http://ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2012-13/releases/201211154w0dbc|url-status=live}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2013}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry |recruit = Mamadou N'Diaye |position = C |hometown = Huntington Beach |highschool = Brethren Christian |feet = 7 |inches = 5 |weight = 260 |40 = |commitdate = 14 November 2012 |scout stars = 3 |rivals stars = 4 |espn grade = 85 }} |} == College career == === Freshman year === Upon joining the UC Irvine basketball program, N'Diaye was instantly recognized as the tallest player in the [[Division I (NCAA)|NCAA Division I]]. [[Russell Turner (basketball)|Russell Turner]], the head basketball coach, said, "I'm excited to add a player of Mamadou's quality and character to our program." On 2 November 2013, N'Diaye represented UC Irvine for the first time in an exhibition game vs. [[Chapman University|Chapman]]. He finished with 9 points, a team-high 7 rebounds and 5 blocks. Turner said after the game, "I was pleased with Mamadou's play. He is a dominating factor at times and he will be a factor that other teams will have to deal with."{{cite web|title=UC Irvine Overpowers Chapman, 89-61|url=http://ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/releases/20131103r1w5ik|website=UCIrvineSports.com|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=17 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140817055851/http://ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/releases/20131103r1w5ik|url-status=live}} N'Diaye made his collegiate debut on 8 November 2013 against [[Fresno State Bulldogs men's basketball|Fresno State]] with 5 points, 4 rebounds, and 1 block as the starting center. He also shot 1-of-1 from the field and 3-of-10 from the free throw line. However, the team lost the game at the buzzer.{{cite web|title=Bulldog Buzzer-Beater Defeats 'Eaters|url=http://ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/releases/20131109x4l07u|website=UCIrvineSports.com|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=19 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140819222427/http://ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/releases/20131109x4l07u|url-status=live}} When the Anteaters defeated the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball]] team on 14 November 2013, N'Diaye recorded a season-high 18 points. He also added 8 rebounds and 9 blocks. The game was also his first experience in the [[2K Sports Classic]]. His blocked shots total broke the school's single-game record under the category.{{cite web|title=UC Irvine Takes Down Washington, 86-72|url=http://ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/releases/2013111508amth|website=UCIrvineSports.com|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=17 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140817062805/http://ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/releases/2013111508amth|url-status=live}} He recorded his first career double-double with Irvine on 28 December 2013 against [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]], with 12 points, 4 blocks, and a career-high 12 rebounds.{{cite web|title=UC Irvine Falls at Arizona State, 74-61|url=http://ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/releases/20131228y71zxu|website=UCIrvineSports.com|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=17 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140817065506/http://ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/releases/20131228y71zxu|url-status=live}} In January, in a game at rival [[Long Beach State 49ers men's basketball|Long Beach State]], coach [[Dan Monson]] told reporters that he believed his team was still afraid to attack the paint even when N'Diaye was sitting on the bench. In early February, N'Diaye broke the school's single-game block record for the second time in the season, totaling with 11 blocked shots and 10 rebounds against Long Beach State. N'Diaye also broke the conference's all-time record. It was his first career game in which he recorded a double-double without scoring over ten points.{{cite web|title=UC Irvine's Mamadou Ndiaye Breaks Big West Single-Game Record With 11 Blocks In Win Over Long Beach|url=http://losangeles.cbslocal.com/2014/02/06/uc-irvines-mamadou-ndiaye-breaks-big-west-single-game-record-with-11-blocks-in-win-over-long-beach/|website=CBSLocal.com|date=6 February 2014|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=29 November 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129083528/http://losangeles.cbslocal.com/2014/02/06/uc-irvines-mamadou-ndiaye-breaks-big-west-single-game-record-with-11-blocks-in-win-over-long-beach/|url-status=live}} N'Diaye finished the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14 season]] with averages of 7.8 points, 6.2 rebounds, 0.2 assists, 3.1 blocks, and 1.7 turnovers per game.{{cite web|title=Mamadou Ndiaye Game Logs|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Mamadou-Ndiaye/GameLogs/41432|website=RealGM.com|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=16 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141216164901/http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Mamadou-Ndiaye/GameLogs/41432|url-status=live}} Following the year, he was labeled a future top prospect by Kevin Pelton of [[ESPN.com]], strongly due to his performance against Washington, in which he broke the school record for blocks for a single game.{{cite web|last1=Pelton|first1=Kevin|title=Mamadou Ndiaye's rising stock|url=https://insider.espn.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10002061/why-uc-irvine-mamadou-ndiaye-top-prospect-nba|website=ESPN.com|date=19 November 2013|access-date=18 September 2014|archive-date=19 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140919235336/http://insider.espn.go.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10002061/why-uc-irvine-mamadou-ndiaye-top-prospect-nba|url-status=live}} UC Irvine lost 58–64 in the first round of the [[2014 National Invitation Tournament]] against [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]]. They fell to [[Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball|Cal Poly]] in the [[2014 Big West Conference men's basketball tournament]] shortly before.{{cite web|title=2013-14 UC Irvine Schedule|url=http://www.ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/schedule|website=UCIrvineSports.com|access-date=28 April 2015|archive-date=27 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150427060326/http://www.ucirvinesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/schedule|url-status=live}} === Sophomore year === N'Diaye debuted as a sophomore on 14 November 2014, recording 9 points, 2 rebounds, and 1 block against [[Chapman University]]. He scored a career-high 21 points on 29 November, vs [[Loyola Marymount Lions men's basketball|Loyola Marymount]]. This was the first time he notched over 20 points in his college career as well.{{cite web|title=Mamadou Ndiaye Game Logs|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Mamadou-Ndiaye/GameLogs/41432|website=RealGM.com|access-date=7 December 2014|archive-date=16 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141216164901/http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Mamadou-Ndiaye/GameLogs/41432|url-status=live}}{{cite web|title=Ndiaye Scores Career-High 21 As UC Irvine Downs LMU, 80-72|url=http://losangeles.cbslocal.com/2014/11/29/ndiaye-scores-career-high-21-as-uc-irvine-downs-lmu-80-72/|website=CBSLocal.com|date=29 November 2014|access-date=7 December season-high scoring total.{{cite web|title=Mamadou Ndiaye Game Logs|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Mamadou-Ndiaye/GameLogs/41432|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=28 April 2015|archive-date=16 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141216164901/http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Mamadou-Ndiaye/GameLogs/41432|url-status=live}} N'Diaye was sidelined for two months in his draft|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/sportsnow/la-sp-sn-uc-irvine-mamadou-ndiaye-20150414-story.html|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=14 April 2015|access-date=28 April 2015|archive-date=25 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150425155236/http://www.latimes.com/sports/sportsnow/la-sp-sn-uc-irvine-mamadou-ndiaye-20150414-story.html|url-status=live}}{{cite web|last1=Moore|first1=David Leon|title=UC Irvine coach: No flopping against Mamadou Ndiaye|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2015/03/19/uc-irvine-mamadou-ndiaye-louisville-flop/25046901/|website=[[USA Today]]|access-date=28 April 2015|archive-date=24 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150324001742/http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2015/03/19/uc-irvine-mamadou-ndiaye-louisville-flop/25046901/|url-status=live}} After his team qualified for the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]], he drew attention on [[Twitter]]. [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball]] head coach [[Rick Pitino]], who coached against UC Irvine's Russell Turner in the first round, said, "I thought he was eight feet tall."{{cite magazine|last1=Taylor|first1=Phil|title=Biggest star of NCAA tournament is 7'6" Mamadou Ndiaye of UC Irvine|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/03/20/mamadou-ndiaye-76-uc-irvine-anteaters-ncaa-tournament|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|access-date=28 April 2015|archive-date=9 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150509023438/http://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/03/20/mamadou-ndiaye-76-uc-irvine-anteaters-ncaa-tournament|url-status=live}} The Anteaters' season ended when they lost 55–57 to Louisville, in spite of the 12 points, 5 rebounds, and 1 block N'Diaye recorded. He finished the season averaging 10.5 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 1.7 blocks. === Junior year === In mid-April 2015, N'Diaye made it official that he would forgo the [[2015 NBA draft]] and return to UC Irvine for his [[Junior (education year)|junior]] year. The school later released a statement, in which his coach said, "This is great news for Mamadou and for our program. He is staying here because he is happy, he's committed to his education and he is thriving. I feel really good about those things." Following his second season with the Anteaters, websites such as [[CBSSports.com]] considered him a player that would need to play in the [[NBA Development League]] before joining a [[National Basketball Association]] roster.{{cite web|last1=Vecenie|first1=Sam|title=2015 NBA Draft Big Board Update: Draft Declarations shake up top 100|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/25143859/nba-draft-big-board-update-draft-declarations-shake-up-top-100|website=[[CBSSports.com]]|access-date=28 April 2015|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304110459/http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/25143859/nba-draft-big-board-update-draft-declarations-shake-up-top-100|url-status=live}} By his junior year, N'Diaye was no longer the tallest NCAA player. He faced fellow Senegalese {{height|ft=7|in=6}} player [[Tacko Fall]] in the tallest tip-off and match-up in US college basketball history in a game against the [[University of Central Florida|UCF]] [[UCF Knights men's basketball|Knights]].{{Cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/early-lead/wp/2015/11/19/tacko-fall-and-mamadou-ndiaye-both-7-foot-6-faced-off-wednesday-for-the-tallest-head-to-head-matchup-in-college-basketball-history/ |title=Tacko Fall and Mamadou N'Diaye faced off Wednesday for the tallest head-to-head matchup in college basketball history |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=28 May 2016 |archive-date=7 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160807204115/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/early-lead/wp/2015/11/19/tacko-fall-and-mamadou-ndiaye-both-7-foot-6-faced-off-wednesday-for-the-tallest-head-to-head-matchup-in-college-basketball-history/ |url-status=live }} During his junior season, N'Diaye led the Anteaters to a program-best 28 wins. He played in 37 of 38 games on the season, starting 36, and averaged 12.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game. He broke the UCI school record for blocks with 218 which was previously broken by former teammate Will Davis II the previous season with 208. On 7 April 2016, N'Diaye declared for the [[2016 NBA draft]], but did not hire an agent.{{Cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/7-6-center-mamadou-ndiaye-declares-for-nba-draft-002156511.html he vowed to continue his studies in order to achieve his dream of getting a college degree.{{Cite web |url=https://ucirvine.prestosports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2015-16/releases/20160524tqylnf On 26 August 2020, N'Diaye re-signed with Correcaminos.{{cite web |last1=Chelidze |first1=Dimitri |title=Ndiaye re-signs at Correcaminos |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Mexico/news/642435/Ndiaye-re-signs-at-Correcaminos |website=Latinbasket |access-date=26 August 2020 |date=26 August 2020 |archive-date=7 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107090235/https://www.latinbasket.com/Mexico/news/642435/Ndiaye-re-signs-at-Correcaminos |url-status=live }} == Player profile == Standing seven feet, six inches tall and weighing 300 pounds, N'Diaye's wingspan (fingertip-to-fingertip reach) was measured as {{convert|8|ft|1|in|m|abbr=on}} at the 2012 edition of the [[Amar'e Stoudemire]] Skills Academy.{{cite web|title=Mamadou Ndiaye|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/mamadou-ndiaye|website=NBADraft.net|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=12 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812052244/http://www.nbadraft.net/players/mamadou-ndiaye|url-status=live}} When he entered college, his wingspan had increased to over {{convert|8|ft|3|in|m|abbr=on}}.{{cite web|last1=Kaufman|first1=Joey|title=The Burden of 7-6|url=http://www.sportsonearth.com/article/67717370/uc-irvine-7-foot-6-center-mamadou-ndiaye-discusses-challenges|website=SportsOnEarth.com|access-date=16 September 2014|archive-date=15 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150915152218/http://www.sportsonearth.com/article/67717370/uc-irvine-7-foot-6-center-mamadou-ndiaye-discusses-challenges|url-status=dead}} He is solely used as a [[center (basketball)|center]] due to his height, length, and size. N'Diaye's skill set was often considered "raw" in high school, and received comments from Brethren Christian head coach, Jon Bahnsen, who said, "Right now his game is basically catch, turn, drop-step, dunk."{{cite web|last1=Smith|first1=Cameron|title=7-foot-5 Senegalese teen Mamadou Ndiaye is dominating California prep hoops|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/highschool-prep-rally/7-foot-5-senegalese-teen-mamadou-ndiaye-dominating-201311480.html|website=Yahoo.com|date=20 January 2012 |access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=17 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141017185902/http://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/highschool-prep-rally/7-foot-5-senegalese-teen-mamadou-ndiaye-dominating-201311480.html|url-status=live}} He is also capable of touching the standard [[basketball]] rim without jumping.{{cite news|last1=Nelson|first1=Sara C|title=Mamadou Ndiaye Is Tallest Basketball Player At 7ft 5in|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/2012/01/24/mamadou-ndiaye-is-tallest-basketball-player-at-7ft-5in-tall-pictures-video_n_1228032.html|work=Huffington Post|date=21 January 2012|access-date=17 September 2014|archive-date=29 November 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129134300/http://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/2012/01/24/mamadou-ndiaye-is-tallest-basketball-player-at-7ft-5in-tall-pictures-video_n_1228032.html|url-status=live}} During the 2016 tournament season, a writer for ''SB Nation'' wrote that "When Columbia guards find themselves one-on-one with just his frame between them and the rim, they reverse direction and scurry away, like terrified Tokyoites who just heard Godzilla stomping around. One fan screams 'You're not that tall!' at him, which is a lie. Another yells 'You're only the 36th-tallest in the world!,' which upon further research, turns out to be true."{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2016/3/31/11331408/cit-tournament-march-madness-ncaa-columbia-uc-irvine|title=It takes $100,000 or 10,000 miles to get college basketball's fourth-best trophy, and to some schools, that's worth it|first=Rodger|last=Sherman|publisher=SB Nation|date=31 March 2016|access-date=31 March 2016|archive-date=3 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403023721/http://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2016/3/31/11331408/cit-tournament-march-madness-ncaa-columbia-uc-irvine|url-status=live}} In the past, N'Diaye has been compared with players such as [[Yao Ming]] and [[Rudy Gobert]], who respectively stand 7'6" and 7'1" (2.29 m and 2.16 m) and feature a similar wingspan. ==The Basketball Tournament (TBT)== In the summer of 2017, N'Diaye competed in [[The Basketball Tournament]] on [[ESPN]] for Paul Champions. Competing for the $2 million grand prize, N'Diaye helped lead his team to two victories in the TBT Jamboree which secured Paul Champions' spot as one of the 64 teams in the tournament. During the Jamboree, N'Diaye averaged 8.0 points, 7.0 rebounds and 2.0 blocks per game. In their first-round match up, he helped the Champions to a 78–74 victory over the Talladega Knights; a team led by former [[NBA]] players [[Josh Boone (basketball)|Josh Boone]] and [[Gary Forbes]]. N'Diaye and the Champions would eventually fall in the second-round to the number one seeded Untouchables.{{Cite web
